title: Hodgkin lymphoma
subtitle: Classic HL vs NLPHL · highly curable, and managed by interim PET — give enough therapy to cure while withdrawing bleomycin and radiation from those who don't need them · N-AVD (US) and BrECADD (Europe) are the advanced-stage standards
source: Compiled from the Stanford Oncology Handbook 2025, Lymphoma: Hodgkin (Chou L, Schroers-Martin J) · NCCN · primary trial reports verified against PubMed, September 2026.

blocks.heading: Classic HL vs NLPHL — two different diseases
rows: Hodgkin Reed-Sternberg (HRS) — binucleate, owl-eye nucleoli; a tiny minority of cells in an inflammatory background
LP (“popcorn”) cells in nodules of follicular dendritic cells, ringed by PD-1+ T-cell rosettes
CD30+ CD15+, CD45−, PAX5 dim, MUM1+. CD20 negative or weak/patchy; OCT2/BOB1 lost. EBV (LMP1) + in a subset
9p24.1 gain → PD-L1/PD-L2 + JAK-STAT, NF-κB — the reason PD-1 blockade works
Intact germinal-center B-cell program — really a B-cell lymphoma
Nodular sclerosis (young, mediastinal) · mixed cellularity (older, EBV+, HIV) · lymphocyte-rich · lymphocyte-depleted
ICC 2022: nodular lymphocyte-predominant B-cell lymphoma; WHO-HAEM5 keeps NLPHL. Variant patterns C–F (THRLBCL-like) do worse
blocks.footnote: Lymphocyte-rich cHL mimics NLPHL on morphology — the immunophenotype separates them. Gray-zone lymphoma sits between cHL and PMBL.

blocks.heading: Workup
items: History: B symptoms, pruritus, alcohol-induced nodal pain; exam of nodal regions, liver, spleen; performance status
Excisional biopsy preferred, core acceptable, never FNA (HRS cells are sparse and architecture matters)
IHC — the critical panel: CD30, CD15, PAX5, CD20, CD3
Labs: CBC/diff, CMP (albumin), ESR, LDH, HIV, HBV and HCV, pregnancy test
PET-CT stages; no routine marrow biopsy — only for focal bone lesions or unexplained cytopenias
Echo/MUGA before anthracycline · PFTs with DLCO before bleomycin · before PD-1: TSH, ACTH/cortisol, troponin
Fertility: low risk with A(B)VD or N-AVD, so preservation is not mandated; bank before eBEACOPP/BrECADD or salvage

blocks.heading: Deauville 5-point score
rows: Uptake > mediastinum but ≤ liver — usually adequate response
Moderately > liver · markedly > liver or new lesions — treatment failure
blocks.footnote: Response is reported this way in practice and in every trial cited. (The handbook itself specifies only PET/CT at completion, plus marrow biopsy if positive at diagnosis.)

blocks.heading: Staging — Cotswolds-modified Ann Arbor
rows: One lymph node region or lymphoid structure (spleen, thymus, Waldeyer ring)
≥2 regions, same side of the diaphragm. Hilar nodes are lateralized — bilateral involvement is stage II
Regions on both sides of the diaphragm
Disseminated — marrow, CNS, or more than one extranodal site
B = weight loss >10% over 6 mo, or unexplained fever >38°C in the past month, or recurrent drenching night sweats
S splenic · X bulky: node ≥10 cm, or mediastinal mass ≥⅓ the transverse thoracic diameter at T5–6 · E limited direct extranodal extension
blocks.footnote: A single extranodal site as the only disease is IE; more than one extranodal site is stage IV. Hilar (bronchopulmonary) nodes sit outside the mediastinum.

blocks.heading: Early-stage (CS I–II) unfavorable factors
blocks.footnote: Favorable = none present. GHSG areas lump infraclavicular with ipsilateral cervical and both hila with the mediastinum. Stage IIB with bulk or extranodal disease is treated as advanced by GHSG (eligible for HD21). The handbook table lists ≥3 / ≥2 areas — the trial definitions are ≥4 (EORTC) and ≥3 (GHSG).

blocks.heading: IPS — advanced stage (freedom from progression)
blocks.footnote: One point each: albumin <4 · Hgb <10.5 · male · stage IV · age ≥45 · WBC ≥15,000 · lymphocytes <600 or <8%. Moccia is the ABVD-era revision. Modern regimens flatten the curve — N-AVD 3-yr PFS was 87% even at IPS 4–7.

blocks.heading: Treatment pathway — interim PET drives it

chains.header: Early favorable (CS I–II, no risk factors)

boxes: EOT PET: RT only to avid residual (0.7% in S1826)

pages.subtitle: Page 2 — early and advanced stage evidence, older adults, relapse, NLPHL, survivorship

blocks.heading: Early stage — omitting RT after negative PET
rows: Non-inferiority failed in all three — PFS lower without RT (HD16 5-yr 93.4 vs 86.1%; RAPID 3-yr 94.6 vs 90.8%); OS no different
eBEACOPP ×2 + ABVD ×2; PET4-neg: 30 Gy vs none
5-yr PFS 97.3 vs 95.1% — NI met: omit RT after intensive 2+2
blocks.footnote: The trade: dropping RT after a negative PET costs ~4–7 points of PFS with no OS difference in any trial. Lean to omission in young women with breast in the field, or when heart/coronaries are in the field; lean to RT for bulk, DS 3, or slow response.

blocks.heading: Bleomycin — when to drop it
items: Pulmonary toxicity in 18%, fatal in a quarter of those; 5-yr OS 63 vs 90% with vs without it (Mayo, n=141). Risk: age ≥40, ABVD, G-CSF — omitting bleomycin did not reduce CR, PFS or OS
RATHL: PET2-neg → AVD ×4 is non-inferior (3-yr PFS 84.4 vs 85.7%; confirmed at 7.3 yr) with less lung toxicity. PET2-pos → escalation, 3-yr PFS only 67.5%
Never with brentuximab (contraindicated — pulmonary toxicity), and don't start it at all over 60 — ECHELON-1 ≥60: ABVD lung toxicity 13%, 3 deaths
Stop permanently for cough/dyspnea + falling DLCO; avoid G-CSF with ABVD

blocks.heading: Advanced stage — choosing the backbone
rows: S1826 vs BV-AVD (n=994, age ≥12): 3-yr PFS 91 vs 82%, HR 0.48. 3-yr OS 98 vs 97%, not significantly different — no OS benefit yet. FDA approved 20 Mar 2026
US default, incl. adolescents and >60. Neuropathy 28 vs 54%; PROs favor it; G-CSF optional; RT in 0.7%. Benefit held in EBV+ (HR 0.30) and non-NS histology. Comparator was BV-AVD, not ABVD
HD21 vs eBEACOPP (n=1500, ≤60): treatment-related morbidity 42 vs 59%; 4-yr PFS 94.3 vs 90.9% (HR 0.66); OS 98.6 vs 98.2%
European standard (EC-approved 2025; not FDA-labeled). Only 4 cycles if PET2-neg. Still intensive: G-CSF, PJP, febrile neutropenia. Gonadal recovery at 4 yr (men) 86 vs 40% vs eBEACOPP
ECHELON-1 vs ABVD (n=1334): 5-yr PFS 82.2 vs 75.3% (HR 0.68); 6-yr OS 93.9 vs 89.4%, HR 0.59 — the only OS win over ABVD
Now beaten by N-AVD head-to-head. Mandatory G-CSF, neuropathy. No PFS benefit at ≥60 (5-yr 67 vs 62%) with grade 3–4 neuropathy 18%, FN 37%
Highest PFS of the chemo-only era (HD9/HD15/HD18)
Legacy — infertility (men 40% gonadal recovery at 4 yr), t-MDS/AML 1.7% after ≥4 cycles. Replaced by BrECADD
RATHL PET-adapted (above); 5-yr ABVD ceiling ~75% PFS in ECHELON-1
Where novel agents are unavailable; PET2-pos patients do poorly
blocks.footnote: No head-to-head N-AVD vs BrECADD. Cross-trial comparison misleads: S1826 enrolled adolescents and >60 with investigator-read response; HD21 was ≤60 and included GHSG stage IIB with risk factors.

blocks.heading: Older adults (>60)
items: N-AVD if anthracycline-fit: S1826 ≥60 (n=99) 2-yr PFS 89 vs 64%, OS 96 vs 85% (subgroup); non-relapse mortality 6 vs 16%; 6 cycles without dose reduction in 69 vs 26%
Avoid bleomycin and be wary of BV-AVD (neuropathy, FN, no PFS gain at ≥60)
Sequential BV ×2 → AVD ×6 → BV ×4 (phase 2, n=48): 2-yr PFS 84%, but 45% if CIRS-G ≥10 and 25% with IADL loss — do a geriatric assessment
BrECADD at 61–75 (HD21 cohort, n=83): 2-yr PFS 91.5% but FN 55% — only for the very fit
Anthracycline-unfit: BV + dacarbazine (CR 62%, mPFS 17.9 mo) · BV + nivolumab (CMR 48%) · not BV + bendamustine (stopped for toxicity)

blocks.heading: Relapsed / refractory
items: Rebiopsy suspected relapse. Transplant-eligible: salvage → HDT/ASCT, which cures roughly half; PET-negative going into ASCT is the key predictor

PD-1 combinations first if checkpoint-naive (all single-arm phase 2): pembro-GVD CR 95% (n=39) · pembro-ICE CMR 86.5%, 2-yr PFS 87% · nivo → nivo-ICE 2-yr PFS 94% if bridged to ASCT · BV-nivo CR 67%, 3-yr PFS 91% with ASCT

BV consolidation ×16 after ASCT for high risk (primary refractory, relapse <12 mo, extranodal at relapse): AETHERA 5-yr PFS 59 vs 41% (HR 0.52), no OS benefit; less clear after BV- or PD-1-based salvage

After ASCT or ineligible: pembrolizumab beat BV (KEYNOTE-204 mPFS 13.2 vs 8.3 mo, HR 0.65; OS not reported). Single agents respond often but rarely completely: nivolumab ORR 69% (CheckMate 205), pembrolizumab ORR 69%, CR 22% (KEYNOTE-087); BV ORR 75%, CR 34%. Nivolumab R/R cHL converted to regular approval Mar 2026
Allo-HCT for fit patients with chemosensitive relapse after ASCT. Prior PD-1 raises early severe GVHD and non-infectious febrile syndromes — plan with the transplant team

blocks.heading: NLPHL (NLPBL)
items: Indolent with late relapses; transformation 14% at median 8.1 yr (7% at 10 yr, 30% at 20 yr; splenic involvement predicts) — biopsy any progression
IA–IIA contiguous, non-bulky: ISRT 30–36 Gy, or observe after complete excision
I–IIA non-contiguous (GHSG-favorable): R-ABVD ×2 + 20 Gy · I–IIB or bulky: R-ABVD or R-CHOP ×4 + 30 Gy
III–IV: R-CHOP ×6 ± ISRT; rituximab alone or observation if asymptomatic, low burden, no variant pattern. Transformed/THRLBCL-like → treat as DLBCL

blocks.heading: Survivorship and late effects
items: No routine surveillance PET after CR — history, exam, CBC/CMP/ESR at visits

Breast cancer after chest RT: cumulative incidence 35% by age 50 in childhood-HL survivors, mantle SIR 24. Screen annually from 8–10 yr after RT or age 40, whichever first; add breast MRI if irradiated at age 10–30 (NCCN)
Second cancers: SIR 4.6, 40-yr cumulative incidence 48.5% (Dutch cohort treated 1965–2000); axilla-sparing fields cut breast risk (HR 0.37). Lung (smokers), thyroid, GI, sarcoma in field
t-MDS/AML: 0.9% overall, 1.7% after ≥4 eBEACOPP (GHSG, n=11,952); median OS 7.2 mo

Cardiac: anthracycline + mediastinal RT → CAD, valve disease, cardiomyopathy, pericardial disease — aggressive risk-factor control; consider stress test/echo at ~10-yr intervals; carotid US after neck RT
Thyroid: annual TSH after neck/mediastinal RT (or PD-1). Fertility: low risk with A(B)VD/N-AVD, high with eBEACOPP

pages.subtitle: Page 3 — regimen dosing, toxicity and monitoring, special populations, key trials

blocks.heading: Frontline dosing
rows: Doxorubicin 25 · bleomycin 10 units/m² · vinblastine 6 · dacarbazine 375 — all d1 + d15. No G-CSF; don't delay for afebrile neutropenia
Nivolumab 240 mg (3 mg/kg, max 240, if <18) + AVD — all d1 + d15 ×6. G-CSF optional
Brentuximab 1.2 mg/kg (max 120 mg) + AVD — d1 + d15 ×6. Primary G-CSF mandatory (filgrastim d5–8 + d19–22)

Brentuximab 1.8 mg/kg (max 180 mg) d0 · etoposide 150 d1–3 · cyclophosphamide 1250 d1 · doxorubicin 40 d1 · dacarbazine 250 d2–3 · dexamethasone 40 mg d1–4. No vincristine, no bleomycin. G-CSF, PJP + antiviral prophylaxis; start dose level 4, de-escalate for toxicity
Etoposide 200 d1–3 · doxorubicin 35 d1 · cyclophosphamide 1250 d1 · bleomycin 10 d8 · vincristine 1.4 (max 2 mg) d8 · procarbazine 100 d1–7 · prednisone 40 d1–14. G-CSF + PJP
blocks.footnote: Cumulative doxorubicin: ABVD/N-AVD/BV-AVD ×6 = 300 mg/m²; BrECADD ×6 = 240; eBEACOPP ×6 = 210. The handbook's BrECADD table lists vincristine and BV in mg/m² — both are errors (verified against Eichenauer, Lancet Oncol 2017).

blocks.heading: Toxicity and monitoring
items: BV neuropathy (sensory, cumulative; AETHERA 56 vs 16%). Monotherapy: grade 2–3 → hold to ≤1, resume 1.2 mg/kg; grade 4 stop. With AVD: grade 2 → 0.9 mg/kg; grade 3 hold to ≤2 then 0.9. Boxed PML; pancreatitis
Bleomycin: baseline PFTs/DLCO, repeat for symptoms; no G-CSF; warn anesthesia about high FiO₂
PJP (TMP-SMX) + acyclovir with BrECADD, eBEACOPP and every BV-containing regimen

Checkpoint irAEs: TSH at baseline and every cycle — thyroid dysfunction 7% (adolescent N-AVD), hypothyroidism 15% (NIVAHL); pneumonitis more with pembrolizumab than BV (KEYNOTE-204); adrenal, hepatitis, colitis → prednisone 1–2 mg/kg
Anthracycline: echo at baseline; dacarbazine highly emetogenic; vinblastine vesicant — constipation, neuropathy

blocks.heading: Salvage and post-ASCT dosing
rows: Pembrolizumab 200 mg d1; gemcitabine 1000 (800 post-HSCT) + vinorelbine 15 + liposomal doxorubicin 10 — d1 + d8
Ifosfamide 5000 + mesna 5000 CIV d2 · carboplatin AUC 5 (max 800 mg) d2 · etoposide 100 d1–3. + pembrolizumab 200 mg d1, or nivolumab 240 mg d1 (after nivo alone q2w up to 6 doses)
Brentuximab 1.8 mg/kg (max 180) d1; nivolumab 240 mg C1D8, then d1 of C2–4. PJP + antiviral
Brentuximab 1.8 mg/kg d1 ± bendamustine 90 d1–2 (salvage only — toxic in older frontline)
Pembrolizumab 200 mg q3w or 400 mg q6w · nivolumab 240 mg q2w or 480 mg q4w
blocks.footnote: ICE: filgrastim from d8 or pegfilgrastim; hydration with bicarbonate. GVD d8: cut gemcitabine/vinorelbine 25% for ANC 500–1199 or plt 75–99K.

blocks.heading: Special populations and emerging tools
items: Adolescents 12–17 (24% of S1826): N-AVD 3-yr PFS 93 vs 82% (HR 0.37), residual-site RT in 3 patients — one harmonized pediatric/adult protocol
HIV-associated cHL: full-dose curative therapy on ART. S1826 enrolled CD4 ≥200 with undetectable viral load (n=16): 2-yr PFS 77.9% N-AVD vs 75.0% BV-AVD — too few to compare
EBV+ and non-nodular-sclerosis histology historically do worse; N-AVD largely erased the gap (3-yr PFS EBV+ 91 vs 70%, HR 0.30; non-NS 86 vs 63%)
ctDNA MRD after 2 cycles (HD21 case-cohort): MRD-positive 4-yr PFS 36.7 vs 82.2% (HR 5.3); adds to PET2 but is still investigational
PET pitfalls: thymic rebound, brown fat, G-CSF marrow uptake, and sarcoid-like reactions on PD-1 — biopsy a DS 4–5 residual before calling refractory disease

blocks.heading: Key trials
rows: Early stage; PET-neg after ABVD ± RT
RT omission: NI failed, OS equal
Non-bulky I–II; ABVD ×4 no RT if PET2-neg
mPFS 42.9 vs 24.1 mo; 5-yr 59 vs 41%; no OS gain
Single-arm PD-1 after ASCT and/or BV
